display.title: Simchas Beis Hashoeva Rally, Fourth Night of Sukkos: The Mitteler Rebbe's Simcha
display.summary_short: A live children's Sukkos rally: the Twelve Pesukim, Simcha Engel the puppet, and the story of the Mitteler Rebbe's weekday celebration that broke a decree.
display.summary_long: A live Simchas Beis Hashoeva rally on the fourth night of Sukkos, a Motzaei Shabbos. The host welcomes the night's Ushpizin, Moshe Rabbeinu and the Mitteler Rebbe, who both gave everything they learned generously to the Jewish people. Simcha Engel, the puppet, interrupts with mixed-up greetings for Chanukah and Purim before the children come up one by one to recite the Twelve Pesukim, with a round of applause at the end. Simcha Engel then asks for the song 'I Believe in Hashem' and helps tell a story for Chol HaMoed, a time for simcha. The Mitteler Rebbe once called all the Chassidim, on an ordinary weekday, to dance with music while Chassidim rode horses like Cossacks in the yard. When his own son Reb Nochum fell from a horse, the Rebbe waved for even more dancing. Later he explained that he had seen a Heavenly decree against his son's life; Tehillim and tzedakah had not removed it, but the Zohar teaches that simcha breaks decrees, and the extra joy removed the rest. The rally then turns to dancing, to break the decree of golus.
display.lesson: Simcha is the strongest weapon we have: it breaks harsh decrees and can bring the Geulah.
